speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You've mentioned having a psychiatric condition and new onset movement disorder; can you tell me which specific psychiatric diagnosis you have and exactly what movement symptoms you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; the timing of your movement symptoms starting two months after beginning risperidone is very significant. Besides the movement issues, are you experiencing any stiffness in your muscles, shaking at rest, or a feeling of being "pinned" in your neck or back?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Liver_Function_Tests, Renal_Function_Tests.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood work and MRI are reassuring, so we can rule out systemic causes. Could you describe the specific movements you see when you try to hold your arms outstretched, and do you feel any internal restlessness or an urge to move your legs?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal prolactin and genetic results make hyperprolactinemia and specific metabolic issues unlikely, so I suspect drug-induced extrapyramidal symptoms or tardive dyskinesia. Can you describe the specific movements you see when you hold your arms outstretched, and have you noticed any rhythmic tongue movements or facial grimacing?

REQUEST TEST: Serum_Clozapine_Level (if applicable), Antipsychotic_Therapy_Review.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal video fluoroscopy and therapy review are puzzling given your history; can you be more specific about the nature of the movements, such as whether they are rhythmic, involuntary, or related to muscle stiffness, and have you noticed any changes in your voice or facial expressions?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal EMG and Akathisia Scale results narrow the differential significantly; given your history of risperidone use and new onset symptoms, are the movements purely involuntary choreoathetoid movements, or do they manifest as involuntary muscle spasms (dystonia) or repetitive facial grimacing?

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal neurology consultation and video review are concerning, as they have failed to capture the symptoms you described; could you specify exactly what those involuntary movements look like, and have you noticed any muscle tightness or pain in your jaw or neck?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia secondary to Risperidone.
